Model selection criteria

Source: R/extract.R
criteria.Rd

Information criteria and goodness-of-fit criteria of one or more gcTMB fits, for the choice between growth models fitted to the same data.

Usage

criteria(..., which = NULL)

Arguments

...

gcTMB objects, or a single list of gcTMB objects. The rows of the result are named by the names of the arguments or of the list, or numbered.

which

Character vector or NULL. The criteria to return, in this order, e.g. c("AIC", "R2", "BIC"); NULL (default) returns all columns. A goodness-of-fit criterion without suffix, e.g. "R2", gives both its conditional and marginal version (R2.c and R2.m); "R2.m" gives only the marginal one.

Value

A data frame with a row for each fit and the columns logLik, df, nobs, the information criteria AIC, AICc, BIC, BICc, evBIC, HQIC, HQICc and BC, and the goodness-of-fit criteria RMSE, ME, MAPE, RTSE, R2, R2adj, CCC and CCCadj, each with suffix .c (conditional) and .m (marginal).

Details

With L the maximised log-likelihood, k the number of estimated parameters (free coefficients and variance parameters, the df of logLik) and n the number of observations: AIC = -2L + 2k; AICc = AIC + 2k(k + 1)/(n - k - 1); BIC = -2L + log(n)k; BICc = BIC + k(k + 2)log(n)/(n - k - 2); evBIC = BIC + 2L/n; HQIC = -2L + 2k log(log(n)); HQICc = -2L + 2k log(log(n)) n/(n - k - 2); and the bridge criterion BC = -2L + n^(2/3) (1 + 1/2 + ... + 1/k). All are smaller for better models.

The goodness-of-fit criteria come in a conditional version (suffix .c), with the curves of the groups including their random effects, and a marginal version (suffix .m), with the population curve of the fixed effects. The conditional versions use the residuals r = y - f(t) of the observations; the marginal versions use the mean observation of each time and population curve (the curves of the different values of the covariates in fform), r = mean(y) - f(t), for each observation. RMSE is the root mean squared residual, ME the mean residual (the bias), and MAPE 100 times the mean absolute residual relative to the (mean) observation. The root trapezoidal squared error RTSE approximates the root mean integrated squared error between the observed and fitted curves by the trapezoidal rule: the integral of r^2 over the times of each curve divided by its time span, averaged over the curves, and the square root. The curves are the levels of the random effect term with the most levels; the marginal RTSE uses the population curves, and the conditional RTSE is NA without random effects.

R2 is the coefficient of determination of Nakagawa and Schielzeth (2013): with the variance of the marginal fitted values vf, the variance of the conditional minus the marginal fitted values vr (zero without random effects) and the variance of the conditional residuals ve, R2.m = vf/(vf + vr + ve) and R2.c = (vf + vr)/(vf + vr + ve). CCC is the concordance correlation coefficient of Vonesh et al. (1996) between the observations and the conditional (CCC.c) or marginal (CCC.m) fitted values. The adjusted versions R2adj and CCCadj are 1 - n/(n - p)(1 - R2) with p the number of free coefficients. R2 and CCC are larger for better models.

For binomial and beta-binomial responses the residuals are on the scale of proportions.

References

Nakagawa, S. and Schielzeth, H. (2013). A general and simple method for obtaining R2 from generalized linear mixed-effects models. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 4, 133-142.

Vonesh, E. F., Chinchilli, V. M. and Pu, K. (1996). Goodness-of-fit in generalized nonlinear mixed-effects models. Biometrics 52, 572-587.

Examples

fl <- gcTMB(height ~ DAS, rform=b1 + b2 ~ 1 | plant_ID, data=FabaHeights25)
fg <- gcTMB(height ~ DAS, rform=b1 + b2 ~ 1 | plant_ID, data=FabaHeights25, model="gompertz")
criteria(logistic=fl, gompertz=fg)
#>             logLik df nobs      AIC     AICc      BIC     BICc    evBIC
#> logistic -513.6748  7  200 1041.350 1041.933 1064.438 1066.185 1059.301
#> gompertz -530.0197  7  200 1074.039 1074.623 1097.128 1098.875 1091.827
#>              HQIC    HQICc       BC   RMSE.c    RMSE.m        ME.c        ME.m
#> logistic 1050.693 1051.793 1116.024 1.817786 0.5654044 -0.01070386 -0.02035558
#> gompertz 1083.383 1084.483 1148.714 2.055811 0.8278522  0.03554012  0.02100574
#>            MAPE.c   MAPE.m   RTSE.c    RTSE.m      R2.c      R2.m   R2adj.c
#> logistic 3.294648 0.651532 1.741021 0.6055063 0.9968727 0.9417571 0.9968250
#> gompertz 3.212344 1.422527 1.939751 0.8204698 0.9960090 0.9418983 0.9959482
#>            R2adj.m     CCC.c     CCC.m  CCCadj.c  CCCadj.m
#> logistic 0.9408701 0.9984232 0.9688412 0.9983992 0.9683667
#> gompertz 0.9410135 0.9979880 0.9686947 0.9979574 0.9682180
criteria(logistic=fl, gompertz=fg, which=c("AIC", "R2", "BIC"))
#>               AIC      R2.c      R2.m      BIC
#> logistic 1041.350 0.9968727 0.9417571 1064.438
#> gompertz 1074.039 0.9960090 0.9418983 1097.128
